scoring_justification: Full recompute from raw artifacts is infeasible for MD in the checker sandbox; analytical restoring force is compared to paper's reported 9 meV/Å (T0) with tolerance, and MD friction curves are scored by structural properties (monotonic decrease, pressure range, near-vanishing at high pressure).

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-reported equilibrium restoring force and critical distance for Xe/Cu(111)
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Fig. 3 and text: restoring force at z_eq approx 9 meV/Å; critical distance z_c = 2.78 Å
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Directly quoted from paper's reported values

outputs.description: Contains the equilibrium adatom–surface distance, the analytical restoring force at equilibrium (proxy for static friction), the critical distance and pressure where anticorrugation vanishes, and a list of force vs. distance/pressure data. The checker compares the equilibrium force and critical values to hidden paper‑derived references, and audits the trend for monotonic decrease.

Static friction force measured from MD depinning, as a function of applied normal pressure. The checker verifies monotonic decreasing trend and near‑vanishing at high pressure (≤ 20% of the maximum value in the submitted series).
Kinetic friction force from MD sliding simulations, as a function of applied normal pressure. Checked for monotonic decreasing trend and pressure‑induced reduction analogous to static friction.

output_contract.notes: The MD simulations are computationally intensive and may benefit from parallel/GPU resources. The agent should decide the numerical convergence parameters (timestep, force ramping rate, thermostat settings) within standard MD practice. The checker only reads the declared output fields; no hidden tolerances are disclosed.
